componentDesc.enrich: Finds what the camera cannot show in the source text and suggests additions, without changing the plot.
componentDesc.extract: Pulls characters, locations, props and the timeline out of the text for the script and asset steps.
componentDesc.split: Cuts the novel into episodes in story order, each ending on a cliffhanger, with a hook at the start of episode 1.
componentDesc.script: Turns narration into scene headings, action, dialogue and delivery; every block cites its source paragraph.
componentDesc.img: Reference images for characters, scenes and props. Once locked, keyframes and videos use them.
componentDesc.text: Text that must be exact in the frame: notes, phone screens, signs. Every candidate is OCR-checked.
componentDesc.ocr: Reads every on-screen text candidate and compares it character by character. Runs free on this computer's CPU; without it candidates are marked not checked and can still be locked.
componentDesc.voice: One voice per speaking character; all dialogue audio and auditions use it.
componentDesc.plan: Breaks the script into shots: type, framing, length, where the first frame comes from, which references.
componentDesc.kf: Three keyframes for every shot that needs a new first frame, following the framing and blocking set here.
componentDesc.vid: Makes video takes per shot setting; first frame, references and voice come from what is locked upstream.
componentDesc.up: Upscales the adopted 768p video to 2K. Local upscalers only enlarge; H3 Regenerate-2K regenerates detail — better, but billed.
componentDesc.lip: When lip-sync QA fails but the picture is good, fix only the mouth instead of rerunning the take.
componentDesc.qa: Face, lip-sync, dialogue and text are scored by fixed small local models; defects and match with the description are judged by a vision model.
componentDesc.music: Scores the scene by mood and aligns the music to the cuts.
componentDesc.sfx: Adds the sounds the video model missed: door creaks, the hit at the cliffhanger.
componentDesc.sub: Subtitle text comes from the script; speech recognition only aligns each line in time.
